overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance metrics show that space and planetary 'What If' scenarios are driving the highest views and engagement (likes-per-view). Specifically, immersive exploratory hooks regarding bizarre planetary environments and extreme hypothetical space scenarios consistently outperform standard static facts. Older or purely informational psychology and general science shorts have lower velocity compared to immersive, high-curiosity space hypotheticals.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (970 views, 18 likes) show exceptionally high view velocity and engagement ratios within the 7-day window.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more high-stakes exploratory space hypotheticals that place the viewer directly into surreal extraterrestrial environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing impossible or extreme conditions such as 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,026 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views, 25 likes) attract strong curiosity-driven clicks and solid like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on newly discovered or lesser-known exoplanets with extreme physics (extreme weather, extreme light absorption, bizarre materials).

weak_patterns.pattern: Static Science Facts Without Narrative Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) generated negligible traction compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize flat psychological trivia unless framed within a high-stakes narrative or mystery micro-story.

weak_patterns.evidence: 12-second to 15-second basic animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' published earlier in the month saw lower recent engagement velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than basic trivia.
